statement: Dynamic Components are components whose attributes and formulas drive size, position, material, visibility and copies; authoring is a Pro feature using Component Attributes.

source.ref: Dynamic component creation (Pro)

superiority: Parametric authoring is available in every edition and is not tied to a licence tier.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/sketchup/creating-common-types-dynamic-components Acceptance sketch: Build a parametric box with formula LenX=2*w; changing w updates geometry exactly.

statement: Interact tool clicks trigger onClick actions and Component Options lets end users edit attribute values from lists or fields.

source.ref: Component Options dialog and Interact tool

superiority: Configuration UI is identical on desktop, web and iPad and generated from the declared parameters.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Set an option through the dialog; geometry updates to the formula result; undo restores the previous value.

statement: A fixed set of built-in attributes controls transform, visibility, copying and component metadata.

source.ref: Predefined attributes (X, Y, Z, LenX/Y/Z, RotX/Y/Z, Hidden, Copies, Copy, Material, Name, Summary, Description, ItemCode, ImageURL)

superiority: Extensible attribute set with typed units.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Set each attribute through formulas; resulting transforms equal formula values.

statement: Custom attributes carry user data with units, display options, and are referenced from formulas by Name!attribute.

source.ref: Custom attributes and attribute value definitions

superiority: Attributes are typed (length, angle, text, list) with schema validation and unit-safe conversion.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/sketchup/defining-attribute-values Acceptance sketch: Define an attribute with an options list; selecting an option updates every dependent formula result.

statement: Attributes expose end-user controls: textbox, list, flags (viewable/editable).

source.ref: Making attribute values end-user configurable (list, textbox, flag)

superiority: Custom controls via HTML panels.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Toggle editable flag; field appears only when set.

statement: Attributes can be constrained (min/max, step) so options stay valid.

source.ref: Constraining attributes

superiority: Constraint violations are reported with the reason and the clamped value, never silently altered.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Enter an out-of-range value; the value clamps to the limit and a visible warning names the constraint.

statement: Spreadsheet-like math functions available inside formulas.

source.ref: Math functions (ABS, CEILING, FLOOR, INT, ROUND, SQRT, EXP, LN, LOG10, MOD, PI, RAND, TRIG...)

superiority: Same library plus vector math.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/sketchup/dynamic-components-math-function-examples Acceptance sketch: Evaluate each function on a table of inputs; outputs equal reference spreadsheet within 1e-12.

statement: Logical and lookup functions used for conditional attributes.

source.ref: Logical functions (IF, AND, OR, NOT, CHOOSE, LOOKUP, ...)

superiority: Full expression language with an interactive evaluator that shows intermediate values and errors.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/sketchup/dynamic-components-logical-function-examples Acceptance sketch: Truth-table of IF, AND, OR, NOT, CHOOSE and LOOKUP over 40 input combinations equals reference results.

statement: Text functions to build labels and names.

source.ref: Text functions (CONCATENATE, LEFT, MID, LEN, UPPER, LOWER, FIND, ...)

superiority: Text functions are Unicode and locale aware for labels in any language.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/sketchup/dynamic-components-text-function-examples Acceptance sketch: Evaluate 30 text-function cases from the documentation; outputs equal expected strings exactly.

statement: SIN, COS, TAN and inverses with degree/radian conversion.

source.ref: Trigonometric functions

superiority: Same plus unit-safe angles.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/sketchup/dynamic-components-trig-function-examples Acceptance sketch: Compare to reference to 1e-12.

statement: SketchUp-specific functions refer to current values, options and nearest values.

source.ref: SketchUp-specific functions (CURRENT, OPTIONINDEX, OPTIONLABEL, SMALL, LARGE, NEAREST, ...)

superiority: Same function set plus a live inspector of the current option state.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/sketchup/dynamic-component-supported-functions Acceptance sketch: Evaluate each documentation example for CURRENT, OPTIONINDEX, OPTIONLABEL, SMALL, LARGE and NEAREST; results equal documented values.

statement: onClick expressions animate attribute changes across scenes.

source.ref: onClick functions (ANIMATE, ...)

superiority: Animations are timeline driven with easing curves and can be previewed and scrubbed.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Trigger ANIMATE on click; attribute value interpolates over the requested number of frames within 1e-6.

statement: Formula operators for arithmetic and comparison.

source.ref: Operators (+, -, *, /, comparisons, parentheses)

superiority: Operator precedence is displayed as a parsed tree in the formula editor.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Evaluate 50 expressions of mixed precedence; results equal a reference spreadsheet evaluation.

statement: Copies and Copy attributes repeat a sub-component in 1D or 2D arrays.

source.ref: Repeating sub-components (1D and 2D)

superiority: Repeats generate proper instances with LOD.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/sketchup/repeating-sub-component-within-dynamic-component-2-dimensions Acceptance sketch: Picket fence: n copies at spacing; positions equal formula.

statement: Snaps adjust to specific size attributes when resizing.

source.ref: Dynamic component snaps for specific sizes

superiority: Equivalent via parameters.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Snap size positions equal list.

statement: Hide scale handles to restrict resizing along axes.

source.ref: Scale handles hidden and stretch behavior

superiority: Per-axis resize behavior flags (fixed, stretch, repeat) are explicit settings on the definition.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Hide scale handles on the blue axis; Scale tool offers no blue-axis grips and the height stays fixed.

statement: Texture handling when scaling dynamic components.

source.ref: Preserving and unique textures in dynamic components

superiority: Resizing preserves texture scale automatically by default, with an explicit override.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/sketchup/using-unique-textures-dynamic-component Acceptance sketch: Resize a textured DC by 2x; texture tile size in world units is unchanged within 1e-6.

statement: Testing in Component Options and sharing through 3D Warehouse; HTML tags in descriptions.

source.ref: Testing and sharing dynamic components

superiority: Built-in test harness runs a set of parameter vectors and reports failures before sharing.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/sketchup/dynamic-components-supported-html-tags Acceptance sketch: Run a 10-vector test table through the DC; geometry extents equal the expected extents for each vector.

statement: 2026.1.2 and 2026.1.3 fix security issues in Dynamic Components; formulas must not execute code.

source.ref: Dynamic component security hardening

superiority: Formula evaluator is sandboxed by design; no formula can read files, run code or access the network.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/release-notes/sketchup-desktop-202613 Acceptance sketch: Fuzz 10,000 formula strings including HTML and script content; no code executes and no file or network access occurs.

statement: Reference for DC authors.

source.ref: Referencing DC attributes, functions, HTML tags and operators

superiority: Reference is generated from the evaluator itself, so documentation can never drift from behavior.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Grammar coverage test: every documented function, attribute and operator parses and evaluates once.

statement: .skc files hold components for sharing and library use.

source.ref: SKC file creation

superiority: Open, documented, diffable component library format instead of an opaque container.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Create an .skc from three components, reload it, and verify definition names and geometry hashes are identical.
